summary: Step loader shows an agent task as a short list of named steps, with the current step's label, a count like 2/4 and a segmented progress track. Click the row to open the full list and see which steps are done and which are still to come.
use: When an agent runs a known sequence, like reading frames, matching tokens and writing components.
When people want one compact line by default, with the full list a click away.
When finished steps should report what they did, such as "Read 4 frames" instead of "Reading Figma frames".
When the end of a run should hand off with a clear label like "Ready for review".
features: Pass `steps` and a `current` index. Setting `current` to `steps.length` marks every step done and shows a check.
Each step has a running `label` and an optional `done` text that replaces it once the step is finished.
The row label and the count crossfade as the agent moves to the next step.
`loader` picks the animation beside the running step: `radar`, `dots`, `ring` or `bars`.
`doneLabel` sets the text once everything is finished, "Ready for review" by default.
The step list can be left to toggle itself, or controlled with `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange`.
a11y: The row is a button with `aria-expanded` that reflects whether the step list is open.
The track has `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow` set from the steps.
When the list is closed it is `inert` and `aria-hidden`, so hidden steps are skipped by keyboard and screen readers.
With reduced motion turned on, label swaps happen instantly and loader animations are cut short.

faq.q: How do I mark the whole run as finished?
faq.a: Set `current` to `steps.length` or higher. The loader becomes a green check, every step shows its `done` text and the row shows `doneLabel`.

faq.q: Can I open the step list from my own code?
faq.a: Yes. Pass `open` and update it from `onOpenChange` to control it. Leave `open` out and the row toggles the list by itself, starting from `defaultOpen`.

faq.q: Does the loader advance on its own?
faq.a: No. It shows whatever `current` you pass, so you move it forward as your agent reports each step.
